title: Beyond Effectiveness: A Multi-Criteria Framework for Comparing Practical Socio-Technical Interventions
abstract: arXiv:2608.20649v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Designers and policymakers in sociotechnical domains like content moderation, privacy interfaces, recommender systems and beyond, must choose among a growing menu of proposed interventions, but typically lack a principled basis for comparing them. Prior work tends to evaluate interventions individually and mostly along the effectiveness criteria, while implementation constraints such as cost, effort and feasibility are often considered separately. We present a multi-criteria framework for evaluating sociotechnical interventions. This framework is instantiated through the case of misinformation, a domain of intense focus for proposed countermeasures. We survey $N=39$ researchers on 40 operationalized interventions across five evaluative criteria: political feasibility, effectiveness, user acceptance, cost, and implementation effort. translated_title: 超越有效性：比较实用社会技术干预措施的多标准框架
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20649v1 公告类型：新 摘要：在内容审核、隐私界面、推荐系统等社会技术领域中，设计者和政策制定者必须在日益增多的干预措施方案中进行选择，但通常缺乏比较它们的原理基础。以往的工作倾向于单独评估干预措施，且主要侧重于有效性标准，而实施限制如成本、努力和可行性往往被分开考虑。我们提出了一个用于评估社会技术干预措施的多标准框架。该框架通过错误信息这一案例进行实例化，这是一个对拟议对策高度关注的领域。我们调查了39位研究人员，对40种已操作的干预措施进行了五个评估标准的评价：政治可行性、有效性、用户接受度、成本和实施努力。我们发现，专家认为最有效的干预措施并不总是最可接受的。
tldr: 本文提出一个多标准框架，通过错误信息案例评估社会技术干预措施，发现最有效的干预不一定最易被接受。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a multi-criteria framework for evaluating sociotechnical interventions, applied to misinformation, revealing that the most effective interventions are not always the most acceptable.
